title: How important is hormonal production for natural bodybuilding?
summary: NH discusses hormonal profile as the most important genetic factor for muscle, but argues that naturals within the normal testosterone range shouldn't worry: what matters is the cumulative time muscles spend in an anabolic environment, so years of consistent training at stable levels keep producing gains. He notes his own tests are only slightly above normal, that total testosterone peaks around 30-35 or later, and that only true deficiency or rare genetic outliers change the picture.

claims.claim: Genetics strongly influence how you look, how much muscle you can build and how your muscles present, but many people wrongly blame bad genetics for lack of results.
Hormones regulate the environment muscles grow in; an anabolic environment with more androgens means more growth.
As a natural within the normal range, you shouldn't worry much about your testosterone levels; the idea that only the gifted can progress is bogus.
His yearly blood tests show testosterone slightly above the normal range and stable since puberty; he is not an outlier.
What matters most for muscle size, density and strength is the total time spent in an elevated hormonal environment; four months beats 30 days.
Just as enhanced lifters don't get massive from one cycle, naturals don't get massive from two years; once puberty ends and levels stabilize, that's when you put in the work.
He disagrees that you shouldn't lift before puberty ends; start when you're ready.
Naturals will never compete with enhanced athletes, but natural hormone production is enough to keep progressing even if levels stay the same for a year.
Two years at the same testosterone level (e.g., 300 ng) gives double the cumulative exposure of one year; muscles keep breaking down and growing because you keep training them.
His blood tests show only a minimal increase in testosterone over the years, not enough to explain the mass he has gained.
Exercise, heavy lifting and a healthy lifestyle raise testosterone levels.
Free testosterone peaks in the early 20s, but he claims total testosterone peaks around 30-35, sometimes 40 or later.
If you're between roughly 20 and 40-45, don't obsess over hormones; just get bloodwork yearly to check everything is fine.
With a true testosterone deficiency far below normal you will spin your wheels, breaking muscle down without rebuilding it bigger, but this is very rare.
Lifestyle changes can influence testosterone, and naturally you can never produce so much that it causes problems later.
Some rare people are naturally high-test and look like bodybuilders with minimal effort; certain genetic overgrowth conditions shorten life.
Don't get discouraged by a friend who is bigger without training hard; a natural in the normal range can progress consistently for decades with proper training and eating.
Denying the importance of hormones hides part of why genetics matter, but the normal testosterone range is narrower than people think and most sit in the middle.

stats.value: slightly above normal range, stable since puberty
